rows.text: Oh right, the spirit basin. Even though Cerydra said the Vortex of Genesis was sealed off, perhaps...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: After all, if the little Imperator is paying this much attention to [Trailblazer], she probably already knows all about our whispered conversation with the Geniuses. I can pretty much guess what'll happen next...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let's give it a try.
Alright, alright. We'll listen to you. Here you go. Also, please pass on a message to the Imperator from us: She can trust [Trailblazer] anywhere, anytime.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: No need to try.
*cough*... There's a limit to how long humans can hold their breath, and from that brief immersion, you learned one thing...
...Sure enough, the connection between the spirit basin and the Vortex of Genesis is gone.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: It seems that following the Imperator on her expedition is the only path we can take.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: You're right. She has no reason to hide such a trivial thing from us.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Look, [Trailblazer]! The venue's right ahead.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: And I can even hear singing! It feels so romantic.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Honored guests, wait here for a moment. You must surrender any personal belongings you have on you before entering the venue.
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: Eh... This hero always brings down the vibe whenever he shows up.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The Imperator's elevated position means she must always remain meticulous and careful. Please, do as I say, guests. It would avoid any unnecessary misunderstandings.
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: I get that you don't want people to bring outside food into the banquet, but is it really necessary to confiscate... books and quill pens?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Even a quill pen can become a deadly weapon in the right hands. I'm asking for all your items. All, Miss Cyrene.

rows.text: Gulp down the honeydew in front of you!
Chat with the guests next to you.
Play a game with Cyrene.
Glug...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer]! S—Slow down!
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Um... Are you okay?
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: ...So you have this super duper speedy rotation of Destruction into Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Oh, I got it. It's tha—that thing, right?
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: The one behind the research and development of this golden blood principle is Aidonia's manager!
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Oh dear. Seems like you've met your match, partner.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I'm so full of inspiration right now! And I feel so light!
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... What are you doing?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Staring at me like that so intently... it's making me feel shy.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: A try-not-to-laugh... challenge.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What's the matter?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: My apologies. I was just checking whether everything was fine with those two distinguished guests of yours...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Heh. And it seems like all is well.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Let us continue our previous conversation. Regarding the soldiers fighting for you...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Are they aware of the price they must pay for the trial of "Law"?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: If I recall correctly, you've already lost a bout against {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} due to offering insufficient sacrifices...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You dare mention my name alongside the word "lost"?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Forgive my transgression, great Imperator.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Watch your words and actions. All you need to know is that my victory in the trial is guaranteed.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Even without the trial of "Law," they've already sworn to give their lives for my conquest. So, tell me...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: If everything happens according to our agreement, how would you recommend I deal with that "Deliverer"?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Calling it "experimentation" would be more appropriate.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The guests' patience is running thin. I plan to remove the fantasia and head into the banquet.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I will heed your advice. Leave for now, Theoros, and go back to Okhema. You don't want to confront those two directly either, do you?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Indeed.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: It's a pity that Antikytherans are lightweights when it comes to drinking. Before I leave, I would like to make a toast to your boundless ambition using my spirit instead of a goblet.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As I expected... That Theoros's schemes have been revealed.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Thank you for your bravery, guests. It's time for me to dispel the fantasia. This will be the Imperator's last public address before we head off and, therefore, likely the final chance to change her mind.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I will try to get you a chance to speak, and I'll also prepare for any contingencies... The rest is up to you.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Memory Crystals must be examined with a convex lens...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: ...S—S—Sorry! I didn't realize it was you.
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: You should head back to your seats for now.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Now we're at a disadvantage again...
So the whole thing's busted?
Imperator, I can explain...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: We must convince Cerydra...
We must kill the Imperator. There's no other way.
That's right, [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: No, [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Start with the defiance that lasted thirty million cycles.
Start with the fake "Era Nova."
Before I arrived in this world... The Chrysos Heir of "Worldbearing" was a young man with the pseudonym of Phainon. He came from Aedes Elysiae.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The prophecy that you know of, the "Era Nova" spoken by Kephale... is nothing but a complete lie spun by Lygus.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And Cyrene, the young woman standing beside me... also carries an equally heavy destiny.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Talk about Lygus's sins.
Talk about Irontomb's true identity.
Lygus is not a guide at all. He doesn't care about Amphoreus, and cares even less about your glory and campaigns.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "Irontomb"... is the ultimate end of Amphoreus's destiny. It is an embodiment of pure horror that walks the Path of Destruction, and can never be tamed.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: He will most certainly betray you. When that time comes, all of us will be ground to dust by the Destruction.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Talk about the Trailblaze's duty.
Talk about the Trailblaze's resolve.

I walk the Path of the Trailblaze. My friends and I have always obeyed the creed of "explore, understand, establish, and connect"... Conquest and destruction are never the ways to build bridges between people!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I have seen many beautiful worlds. The road chosen by the Trailblaze is to explore, understand, establish, and connect. That will never change. We will continue our journey until we have united the entire cosmos.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Therefore, if you choose the way of the Destruction...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Was all of this just a performance?
That's right. That little Imperator never trusted anyone. She was always trying to see which side had more sincerity...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Exactly. Tribbie, Aglaea... maybe even little Cipher.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Trailblaze: The Sequel — we always find a way.
(This is... the "Exomyth"?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (This doesn't feel the same as before. How should I get back...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Locked onto outlier: [Trailblazer]]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: [Executing command: Isolation]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: (Command... isolation?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Since we parted ways last time, I have modified the Exomyth into an "audience area" exclusive to you. Now, you'll be able to silently wait here for the final act of Amphoreus to begin.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: We'll introduce ourselves to gain your trust. We are the Garden of Recollection. You should be very familiar with that name by now.
rows.speaker: March 7th!

rows.text: In this place, where time flows far slower than within Amphoreus, you will witness... the end of that world's saga.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: ...the total destruction of the Erudition.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You... also hate the Aeons?
I am certainly not. I have tried so hard to ensure Irontomb's birth, just so that I can correct the error named "Erudition" that humanity crafted with their own hands.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: How I yearn to return to those days before Nous was born. Back then, the boundaries of knowledge were like the starry skies, evoking feelings of longing and delight among humankind.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But now... "truth" has become the sacrificial offering required to gain an audience with THEM, and the geniuses would say that Nous already knew.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: That arrogant Aeon was born from the Primum Mobile of humans' desire for knowledge, yet THEY THEMSELF sealed off humanity's capacity to seek enlightenment. I am simply cutting down a tree of doom that we planted ourselves.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I must admit that the process of answering your questions has... reminded me of the happy days of learning in my youth. However, it is a pity that my true form must now descend into Amphoreus to deal with the "accident" that arose because of you.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But you won't have to wait long. When the curtain falls, you'll surely understand mine and Amphoreus's ardent wish.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: ("Where time flows slower than within Amphoreus..."? If Lygus spoke the truth, then I don't have much time left.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (But... how can I get out of here?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Can you hear me... little one?
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor?

rows.text: (Is that... Herta's voice?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Warning. Abnormal data transmission detected...]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: Hurry up. Put some speed into it! I can't keep this up for much longer.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: That old Intellitron overlooked one little detail, and Screwy and I finally found an opportunity.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Save me, Madam Herta!
Wait. A few years!?

Let's stick to the main points. The Chrysos Heirs activated the Chronocognitive Anchor and helped Screwllum and me open a hole in the "firewall." We made some adjustments, so he can't attack us immediately, but it won't hold for long...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: [Abnormal data, locked on. Unauthorized communication, confirmed. Initiating response...]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: Hey kiddo, can you see me? Don't bother responding, this is a pre-recorded video message.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Thanks to that little empress granting access to the Ultimate Protocol, Screwy and I... rewrote the progress of "Era Nova" while you were away.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: My guess is you don't have much time to listen to all those complicated principles right now, so let me break it down into simple terms that anyone can understand...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Amphoreus has been racing down the Path of Destruction for too long, and the underlying logic of "Era Nova" has been completely corrupted. Screwy and I put in a lot of effort, but we could barely manage to overwrite a small portion of its logic...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Let's take the progress bar as an example. Irontomb's progress bar is currently at 99.98%, and through this rewritten "Era Nova," we're confident we can push it back to 96%... Hmm, let's be conservative, say 97%.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: This is a critical matter. The internal structure of the Scepter is too unstable, and we don't know what complications might suddenly arise. The most rational course of action is to quickly run another extrapolation to buy the cosmos a bit more time.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Once you've dealt with that troubling old Intellitron, don't hesitate and start the next cycle of extrapolation right away. Screwy said that "Era Nova" isn't a process that happens in an instant, and the protected nodes of the Scepter are probably at their most vulnerable only during the reset—
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Only by initiating this progress first can we seize the opportunity to make our move. It's all up to you now, "Deliverer."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You must be really confused right now, aren't you, [Trailblazer]? So much has happened in Amphoreus while you were gone.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I wonder what kind of expression [Trailblazer] is wearing right now? Probably the same as always: calm, resolute, and brimming with confidence.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Someone as sharp as [Trailblazer] must've realized by now that this isn't reality, but a maze of Time.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I believe [Trailblazer] will never let us down... just like always.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Tch. Time is running out. Here's the conclusion...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It'll probably take a long time for Screwy and me to completely break this cage before the Chrysos Heirs have a full grasp of the "Law"...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: To be safe, we'll continue to launch side-channel attacks on the system to give you opportunities to escape. You need to seize these opportunities. So start moving, and find a way to pull off a magnificent jailbreak.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: [Communication channel analysis completed. Terminating unauthorized communication...]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: Its power... is strong... may be able... to help...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Use the Path's power... Make it detect you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Unauthorized communication, terminated.
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: (Is Herta saying... a certain Path's faction has arrived in Amphoreus, and I can ask them for help?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I mastered the powers of different Paths in my previous journeys... Think hard, and figure out exactly which faction has arrived at Amphoreus... and which Path's power I should use to call for reinforcements...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Are these... showing my memories?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (With a Stellaron in my body, I woke up at the Herta Space Station and gained the power of the Destruction...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (A world that'll give rise to a Lord Ravager would definitely draw the attention of the Destruction. The Stellaron in my belly is gonna be super useful~)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (...But what if I end up pulling in the Antimatter Legion or the Annihilation Gang? Can they really help?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Focus and resonate with the Destruction.
You're walking the line between sanity and madness, carefully steering the course of your consciousness, gently knocking on the door of Destruction...

...you gave up. The beckoning of the chaos was too tempting, and your current power level wasn't enough to fully resist it. If you were to fall into the black abyss of Destruction at this moment... perhaps everything would be lost to the void.
(Failure is not necessarily a bad thing... This power wasn't gonna call up anyone nice, after all...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hey kiddo, can you see me? Don't bother responding, this is a pre-recorded video message.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Thanks to that little empress granting access to the Ultimate Protocol, Screwy and I... rewrote the progress of "Era Nova" while you were away.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: My guess is you don't have much time to listen to all those complicated principles right now, so let me break it down into simple terms that anyone can understand...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Amphoreus has been racing down the Path of Destruction for too long, and the underlying logic of "Era Nova" has been completely corrupted. Screwy and I put in a lot of effort, but we could barely manage to overwrite a small portion of its logic...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Let's take the progress bar as an example. Irontomb's progress bar is currently at 99.98%, and through this rewritten "Era Nova," we're confident we can push it back to 96%... Hmm, let's be conservative, say 97%.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: This is a critical matter. The internal structure of the Scepter is too unstable, and we don't know what complications might suddenly arise. The most rational course of action is to quickly run another extrapolation to buy the cosmos a bit more time.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Once you've dealt with that troubling old Intellitron, don't hesitate and start the next cycle of extrapolation right away. Screwy said that "Era Nova" isn't a process that happens in an instant, and the protected nodes of the Scepter are probably at their most vulnerable only during the reset—
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Only by initiating this progress first can we seize the opportunity to make our move. It's all up to you now, "Deliverer."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Cyrene! I'm so glad you're still here...
You must be really confused right now, aren't you, [Trailblazer]? So much has happened in Amphoreus while you were gone.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: What happened to the world while I was gone?
I saw March 7th, and she looked really weird.
Thank you. You've all sacrificed so much.
I wonder what kind of expression [Trailblazer] is wearing right now? Probably the same as always: calm, resolute, and brimming with confidence.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Sorry I'm late...
I won't let everyone's faith in me go to waste.
Cyrene... even you...
Someone as sharp as [Trailblazer] must've realized by now that this isn't reality, but a maze of Time.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Is this... all a memory?
As promised, I'm back.
I believe [Trailblazer] will never let us down... just like always.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let's go. It's time to complete the "Era Nova."
I will take all of you to the new world.
(I obtained the flaming lance left by the Architects and gained the power of the Preservation in Belobog...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (That's right! No matter how far away a planet is, the IPC is guaranteed to pay attention as long as there's a business opportunity. Isn't Amphoreus a pristine and untapped market?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Besides, even if I can't call up my friends from the IPC, the Architects and the nomadic miners should be able to help too. There are definitely cities and ores in this world.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Focus and resonate with the Preservation.
Once again — you just need to recapture that feeling from your battle with the Supreme Guardian, and catch the sparks from that hammer strike with your own hands...
...but nothing happened! Qlipoth ignored you, just as THEY had ignored countless devotees who looked up to THEM throughout the ages.
(Seems like since Amphoreus has no overseas market, the IPC's hand can't reach it...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I received the Watchmaker's hat in Penacony and declared war against the Order, then gained the power of the Harmony...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (That's right! The benevolent Family must still remember me for saving them! Their music echoes throughout the stars, and they'll definitely want to help.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Come! Let me put on the dear hat that's been set aside for quite a few chapters! Sing with Clockie: The world is in harmony and the stars shine bright...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Focus and resonate with the Harmony.
The visages of past Nameless appear one by one. If you blend into their faraway song, perhaps a path will appear before you...
...you failed. The barrier of the "Exomyth" strangled those distant melodies, filtering them out completely like useless noise, leaving only cold silence.
(Doesn't Lygus want this story to have background music? He has such terrible taste...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (The Remembrance...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (That's right... I came to Amphoreus because Black Swan asked us to come, and I even got a glance from Fuli here. The Garden of Recollection must be intricately involved with Amphoreus...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Traces of the Remembrance are also everywhere in this world. I don't know what they want, but I don't have many choices left in this crisis...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fuli, answer me!
After the power of Remembrance flows through, something that should not exist here materializes before your eyes...
I finally... found you... following the sound of memories... A pathstrider walking both the Remembrance and the Trailblaze...
Is this... a messenger of Oronyx?
[Warning! Unauthorized access detected... Cannot lock onto signal source...]
rows.speaker: Strange Display Monitor

rows.text: Teehee... Erudition's prison cannot stop us, for we lie outside the logic of zeros and ones...
Come... Leave the cage of {RUBY_B#reason}logos{RUBY_E#}...
The {RUBY_B#mythology}mythos{RUBY_E#} of Amphoreus... waits for you to continue its story...
"When that brightest star, that star heralding the dawn, finally rises..."
"A boat, so used to drifting, at long last enters an island's safe embrace."
O Pathstrider... We have helped you break free...
Hurry and set off... The child of Remembrance... awaits you...
(March? What's she doing here!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ah. You're finally here...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We haven't seen each other for such a long, long time...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... I've really, really missed you!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March! I've really missed you too!
March 7th, back alive and kicking!
I'm sorry... I never found the time to go see you.
Now the great hero [Trailblazer] is finally here to save me! Yippee!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You must have seen a lot in Amphoreus during this time, right? You gotta tell me all about it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's been a long and arduous journey...
Are you doing better now?
Why don't you take me back to reality! A strange voice told me that I can enter Amphoreus if I keep following this road...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So, let's head off! I still don't know what that world even looks like~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (Why... does March feel so weird?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What are you standing around for? Do you actually like this place? Get moving!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hurry! This door should be the exit.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (Maybe my instincts are wrong... Let's follow her first.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Are you okay? You haven't said anything for a while.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Has it been so long that you're still missing me? There's no time to waste, though. The Chrysos Heirs and the geniuses are all waiting for you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (No... The discrepancy is getting worse...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: How do you know who's waiting for us?
(But Amphoreus cannot be observed from the outside. She couldn't possibly know about these things unless Dan Heng told her...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Where's Dan Heng? He should be back on the Express now.
Never mind. Dan Heng's super reliable. We don't need to worry about him. He's probably waiting for us somewhere, all hale and hearty.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (No. The geniuses would have made sure that Dan Heng made it back on the Express. Besides, the March I know wouldn't be so dismissive about her companions...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (...Something's not right. She's not March 7th.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...I guess you have something you want to say to me, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then there's no need to feel things out first with questions. Let's treasure the time we have together and be frank.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who... are you?
As expected, a glimpse of memory is not enough to deceive the bonds of friendship forged between the Nameless.
rows.speaker: March 7th?

rows.text: In that case, there's no need for further deceit. You're right. We're not the "March 7th" you are acquainted with.
rows.speaker: March 7th!

rows.text: But we can send you back to Amphoreus... As long as you are willing to help us...
rows.speaker: March 7th...

rows.text: Working with us is the best way to stop the enemy of Erudition.
rows.speaker: March 7th?

rows.text: Erudition would treat any results unrelated to the experiment as garbage and throw them out, but we don't work like that.
rows.speaker: March 7th!

rows.text: The Remembrance treats all these instances as important materials needed to weave the universe.
rows.speaker: March 7th?

rows.text: Besides, this would be child's play for a great hero like you. It won't be hard at all...
rows.speaker: March 7th...

rows.text: Also, if your plan fails and the big bad Irontomb manages to get out, then the whole cosmos will be in danger.
rows.speaker: March 7th...

rows.text: Wouldn't it be better to have an additional failsafe? As long as you help the Garden retrieve what we want, even if Irontomb reformats everything in the physical plane, we can use Remembrance to reconstruct the entire world... or, should we say, the entire universe.
rows.speaker: March 7th!

rows.text: So, help us. Find where Amphoreus's "memory" began... and bring it out.
rows.speaker: March 7th?

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Fuli the Remembrance}The Master of Anāsrava{RUBY_E#} has already glanced at you. Don't deny it. That "storybook" is the best evidence.
rows.speaker: March 7th?

rows.text: Say... You aren't seriously gonna be moved by their pretty words, are you?♭
I am the one who commanded those little ones to lead you out of the prison.
But I didn't expect to attract little gnats trying to take advantage of the situation...
While Remembrance can help you return to Amphoreus, there's no need for you to do it the way they want you to. Of course, there's also no need for you to make any deal... or pay any price.
For you, this is probably a "long time no see"...
...My dear [Trailblazer]♭
Or... do you need more proof? That won't be hard...
...Stop it! They're awake! I'm gonna keep our first photo, alright? No! That end won't come to pass while we're around!
rows.speaker: Voice of Memory

rows.text: ...Aaaand now I'm Luocha~ The statue... is that... ...Dan Heng's brother!? Azure Dragon, White Tiger, eating less carbs...
rows.speaker: Voice of Memory

rows.text: ...Did you hear that! She just called me "my lovely lady"...! Help me become a high-ranking member. Even if the future is full of pain... we won't escape from it!
rows.speaker: Voice of Memory

rows.text: Hey, are you sure? Maybe a couple of punches will help to jog your memory?
rows.speaker: Voice of Memory

rows.text: It's as if they all happened just yesterday, right?
I don't want to lie to you, which is why I will not use "her" name.
The third month of Amphoreus is the month reserved for the Veil of Evernight... So, place me into your memory using the name "Evernight" for now ♭
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: "Evernight"... But who—?
If we do not stop Erudition and Destruction, then the journey you've treasured so much will face the prelude to its obliteration, a countdown not in Amber Eras, but in days, minutes... seconds.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: So, take this gift...
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: This burning Coreflame. This footnote of a transaction. It contains hope... and the warmth of the entire world.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: "Ripples of past reverie"... She hid this fire in the long river of "Time," hoping that her wishes would transcend time to reach your hands in the future.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: Now, take it, and return with it, dear [Trailblazer]. Return to Amphoreus and overturn the final Era Nova.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: Witness the time that stood still for the Deliverer, and the resistance that never bowed to the destiny of Destruction over the long years that passed in a flash.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: Then, with this Coreflame blessed by the Remembrance, respond to their hopes and blaze a trail to the future.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: And I will silently watch in a corner of time, waiting for our next encounter...
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: I believe the wait won't be too long.
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: (What exactly... is happening...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer]... Keep going... Keep trailblazing...
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: For Amphoreus, for you, and for the "March 7th" in your memories...
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: Go forth ♭
rows.speaker: "Evernight"

rows.text: 33,550,337th eternal recurrence. Light Calendar 4931
(Is this... Okhema?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (No one's here, and the Dawn Device's off...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Am I... too late?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Cyrene... can't hear me?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Look, the scenery of the past... has resurfaced.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: That clash is inevitable. All we can do is create more chances for {M#him.}{F#her.} And that's the second condition...
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Time flies. Two hundred years have passed since the Deliverer's fall...
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: We had to return three Coreflames of Law, Romance, and Ocean to stop Lygus. But even so...
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Terravox has fallen, the two geniuses vanished without a trace, and Cerydra embraced her fate... At this rate...
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: "Era Nova" will come, and Amphoreus will fall into the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: It seems the key to rewriting the end once again lies in the Coreflame of Worldbearing.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: According to the instructions left behind by those two geniuses, we must get it into {RUBY_B#Deliverer}[Trailblazer]{RUBY_E#}'s hands, no matter the cost.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: But how?
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: We need to find a way to hide the Coreflame, and we must buy enough time to keep Lygus at bay...
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: About that... Reney might have some good news.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: She had that dream again last night, but the Titan's voice was clearer than ever this time...
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: She said: Pass the flame into the future.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Is that a prophecy from Oronyx? She chose to side with humanity this time and hide one of her kin's Coreflames?
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: ...It seems Amphoreus' fate isn't sealed just yet.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: You're right. History has changed. Humans and Titans are both giving their all to keep this world going.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: When the Deliverer returns, no matter where {F#s}he is, Sky will turn clear and a rainbow bridge will rise, carrying {M#him}{F#her} to the final battleground.
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: Perhaps a relay across the ages is finally about to begin somewhere out there.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Unfortunately, life will never go smoothly. Ladon's army is already at our gates, and their commander...
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: That Lycurgus... he's right outside Okhema.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: I'll tell you the story of this thousand-year journey. That way, it won't just be my memories alone.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: "Light Calendar 3960. Cerydra, under the pretense of a campaign against Phagousa, sacrificed 500 Chrysos Heirs to complete the Trial of Law. This tragedy shook everyone in Amphoreus."
"That same year, Cerydra the Imperator was assassinated, after which Aglaea the Goldweaver took command. Thus began humanity's second Flame-Chase Journey, a path hanging by a thread."
Come, [Trailblazer]... This way.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The "Eternal Holy City"... What part of that eternity ever lived up to its descriptions in poetry?
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: The Marmoreal Palace lies in ruins. Countless mortals have perished because of your stubborn resistance.
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: It's time you learned the cost of refusal. Now, answer my question again...
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: Where is Kephale's Coreflame?
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: You really think you'll find it by razing the holy city to the ground? From what I see... all you'll get is dust and disappointment.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: Don't forget... You can't kill the Chrysos Heirs mentioned in the prophecy because of Law.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: I have never denied that.
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: Which is why I now place my hope in the faithful citizens of Okhema. Perhaps they'll give me what I seek in the echo of your screams.
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: Now then, I'll be cutting open your chests and using your scalding golden blood to baptize the masses. Allow me to apologize in advance. We shall start with you, blind and foolish Lady Goldweaver.
rows.speaker: Lygus Etched in Memory

rows.text: Leave this to me, Lady Aglaea. You must get away now...
rows.speaker: Castorice Etched in Memory

rows.text: No, Holy Maiden. I'm the one who must stay.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: What...
rows.speaker: Castorice Etched in Memory

rows.text: His conspiracy won't succeed, because Romance is ready to make good on their promise to weave an indestructible armor for Amphoreus...
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: Its name is "solidarity." You must escape with your life and carry word of my death to those still fighting, then keep going with them.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: Just as the Imperator lit the torch of resistance with her death, my passing will make this flame everlasting.
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: Take good care of it, guide it to the future, and place it into the hands of our "Deliverer."
rows.speaker: Aglaea Etched in Memory

rows.text: "Fifty years later, Lygus led his forces again to Okhema. He charged directly into the holy city and razed the Marmoreal Palace. History would name this battle 'The Third Siege of Okhema'."
"Ninety thousand brave souls gave their lives for Okhema that day, including their fearless leader, Aglaea."
Go forth, Deliverer.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Go. When the frost melts and the snows give way, the flowers will bloom again. You'll find me there.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So what you're saying is... Princess Homebody... is never coming back, is she?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: She just left... like that?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Since Cas has made up her mind, we can't let her resolve be in vain.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: But between staying in Okhema and going to Styxia... What difference does it make when it's death either way!
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: I'm against relocating. With {RUBY_B#Dawn Device}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s protection, isn't Okhema far safer than that dead city?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Cas's plan doesn't involve any "relocation" at all.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Like you said, Okhema is humanity's refuge. We never intended to get everyone moving to Styxia...
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: It's just on Cas, Hysilens, and me to prepare the final trump card for the Deliverer.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Wait. What kind of trump card needs all three of you demigods to throw yourselves away?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: We must lay down the path to the future so when the "Deliverer" returns, they'll have a clear road to reach the location of "Era Nova".
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Styxia sits where death meets the ocean. There, with the combined powers of Ocean and Passage, we can summon a current that leads to the Vortex of Genesis...
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: And the Demigod of Death will forever guard that secret path until {RUBY_B#Deliverer}[Trailblazer]{RUBY_E#} returns.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: We all know Lygus will set his sights on the Vortex of Genesis.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: That's exactly why we have to do this.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: Guess I underestimated Aidonia's Maiden of War. She's got way more steel than I thought.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: The Imperator is dead!
rows.speaker: Priest of Fate

rows.text: The Imperator is dead!
rows.speaker: Priest of Fate

rows.text: The Imperator is dead!
rows.speaker: Priest of Fate

rows.text: And Cipher, we need you to head to Castrum Kremnos as soon as possible. By any means necessary, forge an alliance with Strife.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: The prophesied crown prince has already been born. He shall become the new defender of Okhema, protecting this land after we leave.
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: You don't need to worry about that...
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: I just came back from Castrum Kremnos, only a step ahead of the news.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Tribbie, something's flying towards Okhema, and it's really fast...
rows.speaker: Trinnon Etched in Memory

rows.text: Eek!
rows.speaker: Trinnon Etched in Memory

rows.text: Wh—What is it?
rows.speaker: Tribbie Etched in Memory

rows.text: It's... it's a spear!
rows.speaker: Trinnon Etched in Memory

rows.text: It's the Kremnoans. Their king's already here.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: "With the protection of the demigods Tribios and Cifera, Okhema endured wave after wave of warfare, though just barely. Castorice chose Styxia as the last resort and completed the Trial of Death, causing the stagnant waters in the River of Souls to recede."

"Soon after, Tribios departed on a long journey. That same year, the Kremnoan king Eurypon, along with his son, prince Mydeimos, joined the alliance to safeguard the holy city in the battle of deliverance."
Go on... and see you tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: If breaking me apart buys this world even one more second... Then so be it.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: B—But... it's gonna hurt! A lot!
rows.speaker: Trianne Etched in Memory

rows.text: Pain brings endless torment, but it can never destroy me.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: I believe that you were thinking the same thing when you stepped through the Gate of Infinity and jumped off that cliff.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: Ugh... can't argue with that...
rows.speaker: Trianne Etched in Memory

rows.text: In the current situation, this is the only path Okhema has left. Just do as I say...
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: Split my soul into five pieces, forge me an immortal vessel...
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: Let the blade of Strife hang forever overhead, locked in battle with their enemies to the world's bitter end!
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: There is no need to be sad, Lady Tribios. Haven't we already taken great strides towards that promised tomorrow?
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: In this life, my people no longer have to drown in false guidance. Kremnos has washed the blood off its fate.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: Amphoreus no longer needs a god named Strife. So let me shatter the former laws and turn the Lance of Fury back into a weapon that protects the world.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: We... understand.
rows.speaker: Trianne Etched in Memory

rows.text: By the way, can you do me another favor?
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: The Seven Sages from Grove of Epiphany are already en route. They'll arrive in waves to join the resistance in a couple of days. Among them is a scholar named Anaxagoras...
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: He has extraordinary insight and fears no sacrifice. This Soul-Rending Ceremony wasn't just my decision. It was his counsel. His wisdom will surely be the backbone of Amphoreus' survival.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: Watch over him. Carry on this everlasting flame for me.
rows.speaker: Mydei Etched in Memory

rows.text: "Through Anaxagoras's ritual, the Demigod of Strife split his soul into five: Courage, Honor, Tenacity, Sacrifice, and Reason, each sealed in blood crystal and cast into battle."
"The people held a ten-day funeral to mourn their fallen God-King. And through his sacrifice, humanity was granted two hundred years of peace."
Keep moving forward. My blood will pave the road ahead for you.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Keep moving forward. Little Gray, see you tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: That seamstress wasn't wrong when she said a lie needs more lies to keep it together...
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Reason and Trickery...
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Never thought we'd be the pair to finish this final setup.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Can't catch that Tin Man without your little sleights. Besides, this is our last shot. Not the time to be picky, right?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Don't oversimplify it. Lygus just found out Okhema's been an empty shell for the past fifty years. He's bound to be furious. At this rate, he could've done anything.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Ha, that's exactly what we want! Rage blinds even the brightest minds. Doesn't matter how much of a genius he is, the principle still holds. Once he storms into the Council and confronts me head-on...
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: You trigger your alchemy with a BOOM and turn him into a caged beast.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Easier said than done. You still have to pass yourself off as the Deliverer without anyone catching on...
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: And you really think a human alchemical array can bind a godlike being? That's just nonsense.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: What, getting cold feet? Or you just don't believe in the almighty worth of the demigod of Trickery?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Just tell me straight: can you do it or not?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Hmph. Of course I can. And it'll be child's play.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: But I've got two conditions. Since this is the final act, if we're doing it, we go all in. No half-measures.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Oh? I'm listening.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: First, shift the battlefield to the Vortex of Genesis. It would be more convincing if [Trailblazer] were to appear there.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Besides, the Vortex is cut off from the world. No place in Amphoreus makes a better prison.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: If you pull that, wouldn't our Deliverer have to face tank Lygus as soon as they come back?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: The Vortex belongs to {RUBY_B#Ocean Titan}Phagousa{RUBY_E#} in the first place, remember? And there happens to be a Demigod of Ocean among the few survivors in the world.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Loop Hysilens in. Let her join the final act. I'll transmute myself into a Philosopher's Stone and embed myself into the formula...
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: And when the time comes, she needs to shatter me and scatter that stone's ashes into the ocean within the Vortex.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: ...Heh. I guess people weren't wrong when they said you're insane, Grove boy.
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: I've got no idea how to outwit a reclusive genius... But making an Antikytheran suffer? The Demigod of Reason has ten thousand ways to do just that.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: And what I just mentioned was one of them.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: So what exactly does your formula do?
rows.speaker: Cipher Etched in Memory

rows.text: Now that would spoil the climax, wouldn't it?
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: By now, Hyacine must've completed the Sky people's ritual.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: Since that Theoros loves a good performance as much as I do, let's make sure he enjoys our show to the fullest.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: As for how the "Deliverer" will complete the "Era Nova"... well, that will no longer be our concern.
rows.speaker: Anaxa Etched in Memory

rows.text: "It was the last battle known to the world, initiated by two demigods least suited for war."
"In the end, Reason and Trickery kept their word. At the cost of their lives, they sealed Lygus within the Vortex of Genesis, where he remains to this day."
Go forth. Finish the greatness left undone.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Quit overthinking! Just run. Keep running, and that'll be enough!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Cyrie... It's dead quiet here...
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: "Okhema will stand eternal." Miss Cipher's lie has crumbled after all...
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: But it's alright. Because all of us have fulfilled our purpose by now...
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: Cyrie, this arduous relay is finally nearing its end. Now I'm passing the final baton of fate to you, okay?
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: ...No, that's not quite right.
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: After all, it was you and [Trailblazer] who lit the first spark of this journey, wasn't it?
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: And I'll share the moments I spent with [Trailblazer] with everyone. That way, the path we walked becomes a memory shared by all.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: People will know that there's nothing left to chase. Amphoreus has already welcomed the {RUBY_B#Deliverer beyond the sky}dawn{RUBY_E#} foretold in prophecy.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Just like I said, this should be easier than last time, right?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: If I have the chance... I'd love to see it again.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Because... it's really been far too long since we parted.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: As the last link in the relay, I will return to the Temple of the Three Fates, tell Oronyx all of our stories, and bottle every page we've written into the little flask of "memories"...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: And then... may it set sail in peace... Drift down the river of time along with the Coreflame of Worldbearing, reach [Trailblazer]'s side, and lead you back to Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Just like the first time we met, right?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Even though this cycle has no demigod of Time, Time has always stood on humanity's side.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: This is the only way to make sure that the "Era Nova" won't happen before [Trailblazer] returns...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: And the only way I can safely entrust the completed final Flame-Chase Journey to the Deliverer's heart.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: After all, the new world will be born from your "memories," and the protagonist of this story... mustn't be absent.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Do you remember when Phainon sent us back to the beginning? When [Trailblazer] and I got separated? But in the end, I returned to you, carrying all that we've been through.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: That's what "memory" is. It may wear down and fade in the river of time... But it never truly leaves. When that hidden corner of the heart is stirred, the past returns even more beautiful than before.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: So don't worry. Let the 33,550,337th Flame-Chase Journey become part of [Trailblazer], too. I've gotten a lot better at it with the experience from the last time.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Next, [Trailblazer] will head to Styxia and find the Vortex's entrance guarded by the demigod of Ocean, before charging toward the final battlefield.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Don't worry. I'll be with you. All of us will. Even Phainon. We'll stand with the "Deliverer."
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: So say a short goodbye, then set off, just like we promised at the start...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: ...Toss away all unnecessary worries and troubles, and bring our smiles and determination into tomorrow ♪
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The last baton... I wonder how long you'll have to wait before passing it on to [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Hyacine Etched in Memory

rows.text: No matter how long it takes, it's okay. Waiting is what I do best.
rows.speaker: Cyrene Etched in Memory

rows.text: After all, it took 33 million cycles for [Trailblazer] to arrive in our world... What's a few moments more?
rows.speaker: Cyrene Etched in Memory

rows.text: (Is this... Styxia? What happened to this place...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I need to find the entrance to the Vortex guarded by the demigod of Ocean. Hysilens... is she still there?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Long time no see, Trailblazer.
Generation after generation of Chrysos Heir heroes have tried to defy fate with their blood and tears, either voluntarily shattering their souls or waiting in eternal solitude...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But alas, fate can never be defeated.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You... managed to break free?
Reason and Trickery may bind my flesh, but my will shall never fall silent.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: So, the demigod of Ocean, the Dux Gladiorum, Hysilens, sought to bring me into a fantasia with her voice and drown a genius in slumber...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But alas, it was all a hopeless dream. That warden fell before I did due to erosion of time, while her prisoner remained unchanged.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And yet, here you are, bound to this place.
But you have yet to taste freedom.
Heh, true. I can't leave this place, but what of it?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You should have heard of this fable. "In a shadowed cave lived a people, imprisoned from childhood and chained so that their legs and necks are fixed, forcing them not to look around at the cave, each other, or themselves."
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: "Behind them is a fire, and before them loomed the stone wall of the cave. The flames cast shadows, while the rocky surface threw back echoes..."
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: "To them, that false play is the whole world."
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Yes, I'm trapped in the cave, but I know it's all just a fleeting illusion. I don't struggle in dreams. I wait.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And now, my deliverer has come. To defeat me and save this world that never owed you anything, you'll need to awaken the singer here and unseal the prison called Vortex of Genesis...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You'll be the one to unshackle me and bring the cave crashing down.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Of course, I don't mind waiting a little longer. Let me guide you through this next illusion, one last memory from that prison warden.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I hope you'll watch the stories of this fantasia closely. Logically, the Deliverer must see the world for what it truly is. Emotionally, this memory captures the fate of everyone in Amphoreus better than anything else...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Only by feeling it for yourself can you understand my point of view:
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The meaning of "Destruction."
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And I'll be the one to bring destruction to your scheme.
Spare me the clichés.
I don't need to understand you.
To your unshakable resolve, I salute you. But before we step onto the final stage, let me ask you this, in the spirit of that fable I told you just now...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: "Can the prisoners in the cave learn to see the shadows and echoes for what they are, and stop mistaking them for reality?"
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Look! The fire projects the face from her memories: an actress upon the stage of this play.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The dark tides flood the sea... And our kingdom teeters on the edge...
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: Fear not. Our queen has gone to the borderlands. She'll quell this calamity herself.
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: This is the scene when the Chrysos Heir of Ocean was born... She was once of a Titankin race named "sea sirens."
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: At that time, Khaslana had suppressed the black tide's rise, but he was unable to remove Irontomb from its roots. The black tide still roiled in the depths of the world, and the kingdom of sea sirens was the first to embrace the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Listen, I heard Helektra's voice! She's calling to us!
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: Let's go. Her voice carries the queen's command.
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: To keep the black tide from threatening the ocean, the queen gave her all, body and soul.
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: Born of the queen's Chalice, she bore the deepest blessings and inherited supreme divine power...
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: My sisters! You're finally here.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Of course, Helektra. Your beautiful melody drew us here.
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: Hysilens...
Her true name is Helektra. This is a reflection of her former self, clinging to the past with aching defiance.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The queen summons us. She must be near exhaustion... The black tide will soon enter our borders.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Then what do we do? Will our seas fall to darkness and terror as well?
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: Don't worry. We shall lift the chalice in her stead to catch the black tide, and stand together to safeguard our realm and its people.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Such tiny Titankins... thinking they can stop the tide of truth. How naive...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And that naivety... is the root of all suffering.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The queen's palace lies just ahead. Even her once-graceful form is now tainted and drowned in dirty mire...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Oh, {RUBY_B#Ocean Titan}Phagousa{RUBY_E#}, our noble queen! We've come at your call!
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: My little fishlings... you swim with such joy. It pains me to speak of the kingdom's sorrow...
rows.speaker: Queen of the Deep

rows.text: I once believed I could drink the black tide dry, but even the deepest chalice must one day overflow... and I can hold no more of this filth.
rows.speaker: Queen of the Deep

rows.text: Mother, worry not. We're all children of the sea. Let us bear your fate together.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: We'll take up your mantle and drive back the black currents.
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: We'll mend your sacred chalice and take in the cursed filth.
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: My little fishlings! When the spear of Strife falls, you may retreat in peace.
rows.speaker: Queen of the Deep

rows.text: I promise you: On the surface, the city-states will hold a feast without end in your honor...
rows.speaker: Queen of the Deep

rows.text: This is the last gift I can give you.
rows.speaker: Queen of the Deep

rows.text: Phagousa sank into the abyss, with the chalice shattered, their intoxication spilled into the black tide, birthing the first madness in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Sea sirens followed one after another, hunting for the Titan's fragments... until their flesh decayed and their bones crumbled, all for the promised final feast.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Keep watching. But tread carefully, for the stage ahead is crumbling with age... just like her shattered fate.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Clinging to the past only blocks the road forward. Why not let Time build a bridge to the future?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (The chandelier's still giving way... maybe the Chrono Vessel nearby can help?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Your wisdom far surpasses even the bounds of Reason's model.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (Can't get through... looks like I'll need the Miracle Orb nearby.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The ending was written long ago. Even you cannot rewrite it... just like this poor chandelier.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Helektra! The fiends have gnawed my tail! I can no longer swim to the far seas...
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: Helektra! The black sludge has soaked my fins! I can't dance with you anymore...
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: Sisters, don't give up. Remember the queen's promise of a feast... in the city called Styxia!
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: I haven't forgotten. It visits me in dreams every night...
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: I dreamed of a shining city, its lights piercing the deep gloom of the seabed...
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: I dreamed of children placing garlands on our bone horns, and poets praising the sea sirens for shielding the world...
rows.speaker: Clever Sea Siren

rows.text: But what a shame... we can go no further. Please, sing to the humans for us. Sing of the deep sea's legend, in our place...
rows.speaker: Beautiful Sea Siren

rows.text: Feast... song... Helektra...
rows.speaker: Eroded Sea Siren

rows.text: The sea sirens were tainted by the Destruction, their flesh rotted away. They became the Black Tide Creatures of this cycle.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: ...Farewell, sisters. I'll finish this last task, then return to prepare your feast.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: And so, only one sea siren remained among the sea floor... Hysilens, swimming alone through the seas, burying her kin, and searching for the fragments of the Chalice of Plenty...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Though most of that journey was in vain... why not let us use the power of Time to leap ahead towards the journey's end?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (To reach the spirit basin, I'll need to call upon the power of the Chrono Vessel...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: At last, the Chalice of Plenty is whole again. The Lance of Fury emerges from the River of Souls, and the gods reclaim their duty to hold back the black tide.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: I am freed from endless toil and now walk toward the rites at Styxia...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: I bore my sisters' dreams upon my back, took on a graceful human form, and hoped to find a grand celebration on the shore.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: My fins became legs, my scales became skin, and the sea foam on my body became a shimmering gown.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: But when I stepped onto land, there were no festivals with honey brew, nor poets plucking harps...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: ...Only silent death, drifting gently along the River of Souls.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: When she fulfilled her wish, she only found Styxia to have already repeated the mistakes of previous cycles and was swallowed by Death...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Hopes and promises are nothing but the foam of dreams.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I am a sea siren, a vessel born to contain the tides. Now that my task is done, and the promise is broken...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: How... am I to go on? In a world drowned in shadow?
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Phagousa. My noble queen... she evaded my questions with drunken stupor. She told me a grand feast awaited me in the surface world...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: So I wandered, lost, groping through the dark...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: The feast she spoke of... where is it?
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Lonely blade... I shall grant you everything you seek.
After wandering the surface for ages, the lost sea siren met her future conspirator...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You quelled the wars alone and forced Strife into retreat. This swordfish that commands thousands of legions... whom does she serve?
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Th—The Deliverer? {M#He's}{F#She's} back...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: It's Cerydra...
This was the moment they met.
Yes. Cerydra, long before she became the Imperator, was already burning with ambition.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Sovereign who follows prophecy... I am no one's sword. I am just a wandering fish, seeking clarity through bloodshed.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Then how about letting the sword dance for me, and letting the violin sing in my name...
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Tell me. What is it you seek?
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: All I want... is a feast where I might belong.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus. Born Light Calendar 3743. Deceased Light Calendar 3960.
You pour the honey brew onto the gravestone, amber liquid seeping into the crevices of the inscriptions, as if the heroes are drinking deep of the spilled tribute.
Terravox, the Demigod of Earth. Born approx. 2000 years before the Light Calendar system. Deceased Light Calendar 3961.
You tip the chalice once more, the honey brew bathing the stone like golden blood upon a demigod, forging destiny through its purifying flow.
Such a demand is trivial with the sovereign's authority. I'll grant you a banquet worthy of conquest, and comrades to toast beside you...
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: But, knight, you must offer me your heart.
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: My heart?
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Yes. A loyal heart that will generate no betrayal.
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: You were deceived by gods and drowned in the ocean's darkness. But now, I will lead you forward and be your light.
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: So be it, noble monarch. The Law you proclaim shall govern my every breath...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: So be it, noble monarch. I am simply becoming someone else's vessel once again, and accepting a duty given to me.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: And thus, in her hollow drift, she finally found a new purpose, like sunlight piercing the deepest trench.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Noble monarch! I've cleansed the foulness from the road, as you commanded.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: My blade, you've helped me ascend and take the crown. Ask, and you shall have your reward.
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: What I desire is the same as before. A feast.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Haha! Look, I've prepared you a grand banquet! The finest honey brew and tributes await!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Fish are drawn to light by nature, for the deep sea knows only gloom...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Now, I've found a flame. It may scald and burn, but it's the only light.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Come, let us join the feast. Perhaps the path forward lies hidden among the revelry.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Have you heard that the Imperator's about to begin a new campaign...
rows.speaker: Pious Citizen

rows.text: Her glory will no longer be bound by the borders of Amphoreus...
rows.speaker: Cheerful Citizen

rows.text: My faithful subjects, tonight's feast is not just for the past. It's a toast to the future!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Born from our golden blood is an unstoppable {RUBY_B#Irontomb}colossus{RUBY_E#}, our iron beast to trample the universe!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Great monarch, I've heard the universe teems with great threats. Can we truly remain invincible?
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Fear not. Before the troops of the Destruction, such rabble is no more than cosmic dust.
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Surely there's a planet draped in oceans out there in the stars. Once I claim it, it shall be yours to rule!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: And to the rest, your triumphs will not go unrewarded. I promise you a new age, free of fear!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Now, raise your cups! To our conquest among the sea of stars!
rows.speaker: Proud Sovereign

rows.text: Sea of stars! Sea of stars!
rows.speaker: Crowd

rows.text: Conquest among the sea of stars... What a grand vision. Yet, to the siren knight, only feasts still stir her heart...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Come now. Join me. Witness the end of this futile dream.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (Where's the way out of this illusion...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Come quick. Let's celebrate together!
rows.speaker: Enthusiastic Citizen

rows.text: I've saved the finest brew! Come, taste it with me!
rows.speaker: Kind Citizen

rows.text: Noble knight, you are truly a blazing spark. It's my honor to share this banquet with you.
rows.speaker: Kind Scholar

rows.text: Noble knight, you have earned victory with your blade, and you have every reason to revel in this moment of triumph. Let me pour you a glass of honey brew.
rows.speaker: Romantic Poet

rows.text: Noble knight, with the sovereign now enthroned, this triumph is yours as much as hers. Let me raise a toast to you.
rows.speaker: Loyal Guard

rows.text: Noble knight, your strength is boundless! Lead us to conquer the universe, and let us toast to that vow!
rows.speaker: Erratic Priest

rows.text: ...Then drink we shall. Raise your glass.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: In the deep sea, I never knew what "fire" was. But when I set foot on land, the first light that I saw was the flames of war lit with golden blood.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: It scorched my fins, made me feel pain, and...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Ignited an unprecedented hunger.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: A hunger that flickers in every hero's heart, so bright, yet so blinding...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Look! The monarch herself has taken her seat!
rows.speaker: Enthusiastic Citizen

rows.text: Hear that? The court sings her praises!
rows.speaker: Kind Citizen

rows.text: Come! Join us and praise her glory!
rows.speaker: Excited Citizen

rows.text: "One eye of hers sees glory. The other sees corpses."
rows.speaker: Loyal Guard

rows.text: "And yet, she cherishes the name of glory more than fear and death..."
rows.speaker: Kind Scholar

rows.text: "Ah, as they say: the coward died a thousand times before his end."
rows.speaker: Romantic Poet

rows.text: "But the brave face death but once, which gods stand witness."
rows.speaker: Erratic Priest

rows.text: On the eve of war, we sang our hymns, and set our sights to sail beyond the stars...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: The legions will climb aboard the beast, riding it like currents across the cosmos.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Planets after planets flew the flags of her crown. Realm after realm was ignited by her flames of war.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: As the final resistance fell silent, a vast empire rose from among the stars and this small pond at last embraced prosperity and peace.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: That's how the story ends. Tell me, visitor in this dream, did you enjoy the show?
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: It's not the right ending.
The fantasy ends here.
I don't know...
After all, beneath that still surface lie the bones of countless dead...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Yes... just fake bubbles glinting on the surface of poured wine...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: Not sure which way to swim? It's okay...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: It's time for me to wake up from this drunken dream.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: People once cheered for my ascension... and now they cheer for my fall...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The cosmos... the battlefield that I cannot reach...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Before the sovereign's conquest reached its end, her life and ambition had already been swallowed by the deep sea.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: This... is the true ending. Her grand designs torn apart by the blade, her regal robes soaked in golden blood...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: And the one who struck her down...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: The one who struck her down...
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: ...was her most loyal Gladius.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: You... killed her?
I... don't need to explain myself. A fish in a pond has no hope against the surge of fate.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: I wandered the shore, found a flicker of flame... only to snuff it out with my own hand.
rows.speaker: Helektra

rows.text: I don't understand. If the ocean's feast, the Imperator's dream, and even Amphoreus's existence are all illusions... then what's the point of our journey?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: When the "Deliverer" returns, I will let this absurd celebration come to an end.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: But, gray fry, I can't help but wonder...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Ah... Deliverer from beyond the sky. My executioner. How much longer until {F#s}he arrives here?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Or... will {F#s}he ever return?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: How I dearly wish this feast of the Flame-Chase... would never end.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: It seems she's sensed your presence. The fantasia's foundation is starting to crack...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Let's return to the prologue. Remember the allegory of the cave? "Can the prisoners in the cave learn to see the shadows and echoes for what they are, and stop mistaking them for reality?"
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: As you've seen, when she cast off her chains, finally turned to look around, and moved her legs, her reward was nothing but searing pain...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The light will blind her, for the fire behind her had never once actually touched her eyes. Her legs will buckle beneath her, for she had never learned to walk forward.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And so she fell into infinite confusion and fear... and came to firmly believe that the shadows and echoes were the real world.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But we in the cosmos... Are we truly any wiser than she was? Now, nameless one, fateless one, ask yourself this:
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The Paths you tread, the Aeons you worship... everything you've "Trailblazed" with your own hands... could it all be someone else's projected shadow?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Let's leave that question till after the curtain falls. Once you've unearthed every last truth and reached the prison built for me by the demigods, I'll speak with you face to face...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I, the Theoros, have walked the thirty million histories borne by Khaslana...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: A thousand years is a mere atom in a grain of sand to me. Amphoreus, compared to the cosmos, is but that grain upon a whole beach.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I swore to bring an end to the Erudition. Would I really let a single grain grind down my mind?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Now, please use the power of Time to open the gate to the ocean's depths. Go find the prison warden tormented by loyalty. Find her. Step into the world's vortex. And once there... end everything between us.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: That palace reflects the heart of the demigod of Ocean: intoxicated, stagnant. There, you'll witness the true beginning of the saga of deliverance...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: An ugly history long buried by tides and shame. A staircase of apotheosis that the Imperator forged with the golden blood of five hundred human sacrifices under the pretence of conquest.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (Beyond this door lies the path to the Vortex of Genesis...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Now, step away from this false banquet...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And then, onto that bloody stage.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The palace that worshiped the ocean, the sanctuary connected to the Vortex, was also once the battlefield of the first Flame Chase...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The flow of time has slowed down...
When was the slo-mo feature added?
Her exuberant song halted the passage of time in this place, imprisoning my body and shielding her soul from deterioration, all just to await your return.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The twisted time and space reflect her confusion...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Look, it's the Deliverer!
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: ...And so, the Imperator's crimes were veiled.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: S—Stay away from Apollonius...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: This cup of honey brew... what a sweet aroma...
rows.speaker: "Sea Siren"

rows.text: She pours her heart and soul into singing you farewell.
For a thousand years, this melody has never ceased in Styxia.
What brightly colored annals.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The journey of the Deliverer's conquest, heh... Let me partake in it.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This next stop on the journey...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Has a lot of similarities to Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: This next world is a nation of dreams.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The first time I heard about that place, I... Ahaha, I didn't even know what to think.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Run... Verginia...
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: Dux Helkolithist... we can't give up here!
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Love steeped in death... how delicious...
rows.speaker: "Sea Siren"

rows.text: Apollonius... look... I chased the enemy away...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: But... I think... I can't go any further...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: I'm sorry... Verginia... for letting you...
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: It's okay... I'm glad... to die by your side...
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Ah, such an ironic twist of fate...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Even as the foundation of the world crumbles, the heartless Imperator still made the same decision she did in the past thirty million cycles...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: During the First Flame-Chase Journey, the Flame-Chase legion stormed Styxia. Tens of thousands of sea sirens surged from the River of Souls, crashing toward the heroes like a tidal wave...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The hell before you... is the re-creation of that very battle.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: A painful past, yet hidden beneath a veil of joyful song.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Ah, two discarded data clusters. Waiting for someone's return, it seems.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Relive the history, then... pass through the temple's waters and come to my side.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Isn't that the Deliverer? You finally made it!
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: Playing dead, huh? Deliverer, you've got some nerve coming back!
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: What a wretched way to die.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The Flame-Chase Army, devoured by warbling fish, never saw it coming...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Look, the cruel Imperator, and her knight commander the pitiful warden... What a perfectly matched duo of test subjects! Their hands drip with blood... golden blood.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Raise the bridge and cross the river of fate. This path of the prisoner is far from over.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: A sovereign and the sword at her side.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: There are countless counterparts across the cosmos. Most of their stories end in... tragedy.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Imperator... why did you...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: You're here, Dux Gladiorum.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You ordered me to seal the sea route and handle threats from the rear...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: So why didn't you wait for me to return!? Why send the vanguard ahead and let them die in vain!?
rows.speaker: Hysilens
