rows.text: Die in vain? No, you're wrong. Their golden blood won't be spilled for nothing. The other dukes have paved the road for me to become the god of Law.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: ...The Trial of Law? You never spoke of this to anyone. What is...?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: The one who wishes to bear Law must purge this world of its curse, and offer the blood of the accursed as sacrifice...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I pondered long on what Talanton meant by "blood of the accursed." Then, I found the answer...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You, I, and every Chrysos Heir summoned by the prophecy are the accursed ones. Just like that arrogant Theoros said, our golden blood is the agent of Destruction, the antithesis of the world's fate.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Dux Fragoris, Dux Brumalis, Dux Helkolithist... their fate was sealed at that moment. Dying on a glorious campaign was the final gift I could give them.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You speak as if they didn't die because of your cold-blooded schemes. Was their loyalty meaningless to you!?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Losses are a constant on the Flame-Chase journey, among which even life itself holds little value.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: If a subject marches to war without that conviction... then yes, as you said, shallow loyalty means nothing.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: ...And what about my loyalty, Cerydra?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: You sent me away under the pretense of guarding the rear. Was there... any shred of humanity left in you?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Because you still have a duty no one else can bear. Only you can uphold Phagousa's divine authority.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The choice is yours now. Cast off the chains of loyalty and drive those blades through my heart. Or... stand with me, and sever the ocean's last breath.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: If you no longer share my vision or believe in the new Law I seek to weave for Amphoreus, then go on and end me...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The Imperator of Amphoreus may be ruthless and cruel, but never a hypocrite. When I say "life itself holds little value."
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Know this: I am ready to sacrifice everything for the ambition to conquer the sea of stars!
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Now you've seen it: The brutal Imperator was willing to spill the blood of five hundred heroes to complete the Trial of Law. As for my poor warden... her suffering had only just begun.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: So... what did Hysilens choose?
Is Cerydra... still alive?
I'm no storyteller. I have no duty nor interest in filling in the history you've missed.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I just want you to witness the monstrous choice the Imperator made before the Chrysos Heir turned their blades against me.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Why are you showing me this?
You think I'd falter because of this?
They're nowhere near as bad as you.
Heh... I gave up on using words to solve conflicts two thousand years ago...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Heh... you jest. I gave up on using words to solve conflicts two thousand years ago...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Heh... you've always had a flair for lightening the mood, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I gave up on using words to solve conflicts two thousand years ago...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But I won't squander a chance, not even a sliver of one. If there's even a crack in the walls of your conviction...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Then my victory is already assured.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Now that the past is settled, let's turn the page and bring Time back to the present...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And dive deeper still until we reach the very bottom of the abyss.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The fleet that rode the waves was dragged down into the deep... the flame-chasing nymphs were reduced to ash... what a tragedy.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And you, Deliverer, shall bear witness to this golden death.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: (Is the path ahead underwater? I need the Oronyx Orb to bring back the Chrono Vessel from the past...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Shatter the vessel of time, and let this stagnant pool start to flow again...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Just like the broken fate of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: This hidden gate leads to the Vortex...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Hurry now... the time of our reunion draws near, Deliverer.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Now this cruel journey...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Will reach its end at long last.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: You've been silent a long while, Dux Gladiorum... starting to doubt your decision?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Save your breath. The Vortex of Phagousa lies just ahead.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: After the trial... there's nothing left between us.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: So you'll stop swimming toward the stars, Dux Gladiorum?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I was always a creature of the sea. The stars in the sky... were never meant for me.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Look, a gravestone...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: But whose name does it bear?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: It was here that the prisoner, who thinks herself the prison warden, made her choice...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Witness, listen... and awaken.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Dux Gladiorum... I've lost count of how many times you've stood here over the past centuries.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: You talk too much for a prisoner, Lycurgus.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Two geniuses who defied "Law" and all the Chrysos Heirs who sacrificed themselves in this cycle worked together to chip away my strength, but they — you — can never affect my will.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: And as long as my will remains intact, I am free.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Heh... don't get ahead of yourself. I still have ways to chain your divine soul.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Please. Do surprise me. But I'd say, your mission is nearly done here, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: It was here you gorged out the Coreflame of Ocean from Phagousa's body. It was here you and that Imperator both completed apotheosis, becoming pillars of Amphoreus. And after that...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: You drove your blade into her heart, a loyal subject turned regicide, a demigod committing deicide, or so the history books paint that tragedy.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: But if that's the truth, then why, after a thousand years, are you still here, guarding the Imperator's grave? Still bound by loyalty?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Come to think of it... perhaps I'm not the only one imprisoned here.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Your calm does stir the rage in me... As if the one paying the price here isn't you, but us, the ones who lost everything.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Hehe... That's only because I've waited thirty million lifetimes for my vision to be realized. Countless millennia.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Light Calendar 3960, at the end of the campaign against Phagousa
Loneliness never once showed me its fatal side. In fact, for a prisoner of the cave, it's more like an old friend. One that helps me think.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: But you're different, Dux Gladiorum. Loneliness has crept from the silent depths, sinking its claws into your mind. Bit by bit, it's peeling you apart... Will you regress into one of those lost, mad sirens? Oh, what a shame that would be...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: You're right, Lycurgus. Loyalty, curse, the fall of my kin, and this endless waiting... these shackles are too heavy for a fish that cannot perceive any light.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: I can't break free of the whirlpool that's pulling me under. Nor do I have the unwavering resolve to force myself to wait for that person's return, as everyone hoped for.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: I don't know. And I doubt anyone does.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Then, what will you do?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Memory

rows.text: Cerydra...
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: This will be the last time I carry out your decree.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Ever since you took me under your banner and made me the Dux Gladiorum, my music has belonged to others. Time and time again, I used the siren's song to lure the unwary into illusions for your schemes and strategies...
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Now... let the siren "Helektra" sing for herself. Let me step into an endless dream of my own making.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: O great ocean! I offer you the rest of my clarity and my freedom, in exchange for the strength to stand against the "Nihility"... and honor the sacrifices of the fallen heroes.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Gray Fry, Deliverer from beyond the sky...
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: When you ride the current of time and find your way here, you'll hear my solo. It will guide you to the heart of this world.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: By then, I may still be lost in my self-wrought slumber. But I'll uphold my part of this long relay and guard the shackles that seal the Theoros.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Do you still remember? To awaken someone from a siren's voice, you'll need...
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: Phagousa's Honeydew...
The gift I once gave you... May you still have it when the time comes.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: When you return, please pour that honey brew upon this grave.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: It holds the story of all of our struggles and sacrifices. May you see it one day, the prelude Amphoreus wrote for your return, carried forward through a thousand-year relay.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: When your mourning ends, I'll likely wake from my dream as well. Then, follow the trail of echoes and find me.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: And together, we'll bring judgment upon the sinner who defiled the Erudition.
rows.speaker: Hysilens's Memory

rows.text: At long last... 33,550,336 cycles and 4,931 years later, Amphoreus' final curtain is ready to fall.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: The shadows within the cave gave everything, yet all they did was mimic "life" outside its walls. A futile effort steeped in sorrow.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Enough! They were no shadows...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Everything they did shattered the darkness of this cave and unearthed the Coreflame of Trailblaze...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And now, with that Coreflame, I'll light the dawn of Amphoreus!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Heh. Do you still choose the will of the Paths as your answer in the end?
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: I do not agree with that answer, but I respect your tribute to them. Allow me to take back my earlier words.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: As an apology, and in the name of Theoros who saw all destinies in this world, let me join you in mourning. Let us bid farewell to the heroes who sleep here...
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: And then, let us face each other and decide whose flame will rise with this new dawn.
rows.speaker: Lygus's Voice

rows.text: Libate for the heroes of the first Flame-Chase Journey.
Libate for the heroes of the second Flame-Chase Journey.
This world and I shall halt here... until we meet again.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: The last demigod... I'm here.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Go forth. For the hopes of humankind!
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Go forth. For the duty of deliverance!
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: Go forth. For the belief in Flame-Chase!
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: Go forth. For the golden blood's glory!
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: Go forth...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Little Gray Fry... Please, accept my thanks.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I was the only one left after the world was destroyed, and I maintained this lonesome feast with my songs. I have prayed to that {RUBY_B#Amphoreus's sky}lightless sea{RUBY_E#} for centuries, hoping it would reply to me, yet the emptiness never answered...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Thankfully, you arrived as promised, and everyone's wait was not in vain.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Your long wait must have felt like torture.
Are you still holding it together?
Your song is beautiful.
To see a single trace of light in the abyss of futility was already my greatest consolation. When compared to those who have been forgotten... I have no right to complain about my torment.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Even though madness claws at my mind, my sword stays sharp, my hands agile. If I can uphold this last battlefield, clarity is but an afterthought.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Thank you, final audience of mine... Heh. This is probably the last praise I'll ever hear in my life.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Now... You and I will walk towards the end of this world.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: The heroes have waited for this moment for far too long. Let us use our blades to testify our resolve.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: O prisoner of the seas, Theoros carrying thirty million cycles' of sin, slave of Erudition...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Show yourself! The Deliverer has returned, and the time of your execution draws near.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Alas, prisoners will always be prisoners, blind to the very chains that bind them.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As the only other existence with free will in this world, I express regret toward your choice, but I shall retain your right to express yourself. After all, every actor should have a final line before they bow out.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: It's time to end everything.
The demigods defeated you, clown.
For a narrator, you're awfully talkative.
I eagerly look forward to it. The last dusk this world will ever see shall become the climax that decides the fate of the cosmos. Oh, what an appropriate end.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The Amphorean demigods used every ounce of their strength to constrain me here, yet regrettably...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Allow me to correct your statement: "constrain" does not mean "defeated," and for heroes like yourself, that nuance could make all the difference...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Trust me. This will be the final scene. The last dusk this world will ever see shall become the climax that decides the fate of the cosmos. What an appropriate end.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: My cognition resides in the Exomyth. It is pointless to defeat my avatar, projected into the experiment. My body is the shadow cast on the wall by the fire, and my words are lingering echoes within the cave.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: How can a character in the play fight against the audience? Khaslana failed. The demigods' sacrifices were pointless. As for the two geniuses you placed such high hopes on...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I ask of you: where are they now?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Light Calendar 3960, after the Imperator was assassinated
Confusion and epiphany always go hand in hand. That's particularly true for geniuses.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You must be very confused about why you could not gain a straightforward victory in a world constructed by an ordinary Intellitron.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: An ordinary Intellitron? Cut the pretence, Senior Society Member.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: We've torn off your meticulous mask and figured out Amphoreus's true form: It's part of the primordial Prototype Machine, the first Scepter ever created... In other words, a detached part of Nous's divine corpus.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: That's why it has the potential to destroy Erudition. As for who would be able to control the Aeonic system to rewrite knowledge...
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: ...Only one person has ever managed such a feat.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: You better have an explanation for the Society. We want an actual answer, not another prolonged metaphor to cover up the truth.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Why are "you" the one doing this? Answer me!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Since things have reached this point, I'll give you two a rational answer, purely as a courtesy to posterity.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The answer is obvious, so there's no need to say that name out loud. The cosmos made a mistake in calling me a genius. I do not possess more wisdom than those who came after me. I was just the first to touch upon the {RUBY_B#the "Imaginary Tree" theory}universe's border{RUBY_E#}, and the first to define {RUBY_B#Primum Mobile}"the prime mover of life"{RUBY_E#} with incorrect logic.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Amphoreus is a miniature of the cosmos, where all are born prisoners inside the nutshell called the universe. Like the madman who returned to the cave and preached about the daylight to his fellow prisoners, my greatest sorrow is that I led my peers down a road that plunges into the abyss, from which there is no return...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...I led them into a lightless cage called "Paths."
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I created a Mechanical God that even I cannot control, and then... THEY became an unparalleled nightmare through THEIR endless extrapolations and evolutions.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: THEY bore the name of Erudition, yet THEY tried to define "the known" and to seal off all "possibilities." No new rules were ever born after THEIR ascension, and humanity will forever be shackled within the cave known as "Aeons."
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Therefore, as my organic life neared its end, I coded my consciousness using quatorzain algebraic expressions and spread my logic core over nine bodies, all to finalize my ultimate denial of Nous in the future and to erase my wrongs with my own hands.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As for Lycurgus, he is only one of these nine vessels.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: What an astounding strength of will. As a fellow pathstrider of Erudition, I fully understand your obsession with seeking the truth.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Therefore, you surely see it... you cannot possibly stand up to me in this algebraic world sharing its origin with Nous.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: However, I hereby speak for all sentient lifeforms: we will never allow such a cruel atrocity to occur.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: You can pile on your metaphors mountain-high, but they won't change the act you're committing. The Irontomb out there in the cosmos is still a technical beta version, and yet it's already powerful enough to corrupt the life logic of all inorganic worlds.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: In other words, when the Lord Ravager within Amphoreus becomes the next Knowledge Singularity... There's no way you wouldn't have grasped the consequences, First Genius, is there?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Of course I am fully aware. I don't mind answering you one last time before I thoroughly exile you from this world:
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: My grandiose vision for the future is this: whether organic or inorganic, every act of any life-form infected by the Irontomb will become a true random function. If one were to compute their integral across the breadth of the cosmos, one would obtain a marvelous constant...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Ω — What I call "The Fall of Erudition."
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Then, within the infinity nurtured by that constant, a new universe shall bud in the chaos. A universe that cannot be predicted... and not shackled by the Erudition.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As the first prisoner to awaken in the cave, I must lead the others who are blind back onto the right path and reach true sunlight.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Do you understand me now? As Khaslana stated, "Destruction" is not the process, but the outcome...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: It is revolution through complete annihilation... and the grand rebirth after all has been reduced to ash.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I'll never agree with your views.
That's not a reason for you to toy with fate.
Shut it! That's not what Phainon believed at all.
The Amphoreans already answered long ago: be it as a tiny fish destined to be swallowed, or as a giant whale poised for a magnificent descent...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: We will all fight against fate till our last breath. That includes me, Helektra, once the Imperator's subject, now the Deliverer's blade!
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Such noble chivalry. Admirable.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I will also show my true self to you on this momentous occasion as a gesture of respect, and provide an insignificant academic suggestion.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Thus speaks Genius Society #1, Zandar One Kuwabara, the {RUBY_B#Prime Mover}Entelechy{RUBY_E#} of the universe's Alpha and Omega...
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: There's no need to rage against the truth. The value of any formula resides only in its answer.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: As for the process of solving it... No matter how elegant, violent, solemn, or humorous...
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: It is all utterly meaningless.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Light Calendar 3960, after the feast
Long time no see, Cyrene.
Of course I missed you. It's good to see you're doing well.
I didn't miss you. I had more important things to think about.
Yep. A thousand years was suuuch a long time...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Same here. I've been waiting for [Trailblazer] for a thousand years...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I see. After all, your burden sure is heavy, [Trailblazer]. You're carrying the weight of the entire world...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: [Trailblazer] probably already knew about the geniuses' plans from that "memory." I had to hide really well in a corner in Time so Lygus wouldn't find me, and wait for the right opportunity.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Come. Let's defeat Lygus together.
I'm not sure what to do. It's up to you...
Don't let your guard down. Be prepared for the worst.
Yep! By the way, speaking of "joining hands"...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Not a problem! [Trailblazer] can just relax. By the way, speaking of "joining hands"...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: [Trailblazer] is always so serious, and that's why you always feel so reassuring. By the way, speaking of "joining hands"...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Can I please do something before we go on stage? ♪
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Remember the joke we made back at the Grove, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Look.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Aren't my hands pretty now?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: What a fascinating feeling... Like countless memories all swelling up at once.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: What about you, [Trailblazer]? What did you feel when we touched each other?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I see an awakened human who has mistakenly taken fallacies as truths, and has returned to the cave to try to bring {M#his}{F#her} friends into the sunlight {F#s}he once bathed in...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You feel very tangible. Very real.
I'm a bit nervous...
It's just a hand. No biggie.
Really? That makes me really happy! If memories can move people, then it must've been a happy memory, right?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Are you nervous? Me too, actually. [Trailblazer] and I weren't so reserved around each other when I was still Mem.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Human interactions are truly fascinating.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Hahaha, [Trailblazer] is way too honest! But that innocence is what makes you so uniquely charming.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I'm gonna make it sound more romantic. It means even a bond formed over one touch is enough to transcend space-time.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Now, please remember what you're feeling right now, write it down in your "heart," and keep it there.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Memories you want to treasure will never fade away. Even if immersed in the long river of time, these memories will still leave traces of their existence.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: So, if the view in your memory ever grows fuzzy, just reach out and touch it.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: It's like reading bedtime stories together at night. It wipes away the chill of passing time, sharpens the outline of memory, and restores its power to nourish the spirit.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Now, I'll carry this power with me... and for a little while, I must part from you, as I step into the long cycles of this world.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Give me your blessings, [Trailblazer]. Then...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let that bright future be "As We Have Written" ♪
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Even the authority of Time cannot command the entire Scepter, nor can it plunge the Amphorean extrapolation into a loop...
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: If this was no system malfunction, then was I implanted with a memetic entity of the Remembrance?
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: You guessed it right away! As expected from someone people call the First Genius.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I'm gonna keep doing what I just did if you don't stop, you know? [Trailblazer] and I won't allow you to leave this "memory" no matter what happens...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Which means you are now trapped, Lord Zandar.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: An elegant idea and an exquisite execution. Regrettably, it is you who are restrained by time, not me.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Know that patience is my greatest weapon. "Waiting" and "victory" are the same for me.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Is this...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: You will crumble before I do in this moment stretched out to an eternity, just like Khaslana will. Yet all I need to do is to wait, as yet another futile bug falls down the cliff and into the bottomless abyss.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Now I'm a pink bug? My looks are seriously changing all the time...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: But you're not wrong. We're definitely not gonna solve the problem if we just put you in another prison.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: So that's why we never wanted to do that in the first place!
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I shall answer your confusion purely out of my respect for those who came before me. Have you heard of the Synesthesia Dreamscape in the Asdana system? Interestingly, in the distant past, that place once had a prison, too.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: Lifeforms living in that environment abundant with memoria have a chance to connect their perceptions with each other's. Even across great spatial divides, they're able to detect shifts in one another's states. I call this phenomenon "Memory Zone Entanglement."
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: In Asdana, people made use of that phenomenon to build a nation within a dream... after adding in the catalysts of the Harmony and Remembrance, that is.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: {M#He}{F#She} didn't say anything back then, right?
Is that how you walked into my prison cell? Using those same principles?
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: I would much rather call this location "our negotiation table," Lord Zandar. Nonetheless, your hypothesis is correct. We happen to have an ally skilled in "tuning," while [Trailblazer] and Miss Cyrene...
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: ...both have an astonishing amount of resolve, which I'm sure you can testify to. I am also sure that with the support of such a resolute memosprite, our conversation can last for a long, long time.
rows.speaker: Screwllum

rows.text: I'm the best at "listening to stories," you know.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I'll leave the exciting clash of the Erudition to you two geniuses.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: A brainstorm? I like it. And it's two against one? I like it even more.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Let's talk, Zandar. Take a guess. How much do you reckon we can dig out of your brain before the next second? And how many ways can we find to deal with you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Besides, in your current predicament, there's no way you can take our {RUBY_B#Trailblazer}trump card{RUBY_E#} away.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Go, little one. Go overturn the "Era Nova"!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Lycurgus... disappeared?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: ...Heh, it seems you had conducted a secret hunt in the depths that even I cannot reach.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: What brightly colored annals.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The journey of the Deliverer's conquest, heh... Let me partake in it.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This next stop on the journey...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Has a lot of similarities to Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: This next world is a nation of dreams.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The first time I heard about that place, I... Ahaha, I didn't even know what to think.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: In that case... go, swim onward and give this campaign a fitting end.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I shall send you off with my song, gray fry. May this song penetrate time... and become the prelude to the new world.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Dux Gladiorum, you have completed your duty.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: A new dawn is about to rise. Why not swim towards it?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You died long ago, Imperator. Depart from my mind.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: But your duty towards the Imperator did not die with me.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: That duty will bind you no more. You will be able to hold for yourself one grandiose feast after another in the endless days to come.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: So go. Go and swim towards that ocean beyond the sky with the Deliverer.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: A page out of that sidekick's book. I commanded her to gift this page to you when everything finally reaches the end.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: What's on this page?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Memories. Lifelike memories.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: That sidekick found me after the bloody feast a thousand years ago and showed me her diary.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I saw within that notebook...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Light Calendar 3960, before the campaign against Phagousa
Is this... that Deliverer's experience? It's truly immersive.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: People beyond the sky apparently utilize this power to seal past scenery into crystals they call "Light Cones."
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: But I only know so much about the Remembrance, so I can't completely replicate the past... But I'll do my best to talk about the missing parts.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Heh. I'm all ears. Go on then. Do your best. But if your chatter gets too boring or if I deem it offensive, then Law will become forever beyond your reach.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Got it! I'm sure you'll find this to your liking. After all... It's human nature to want to embark on a journey into the unknown.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Is this... A fortress in the sky?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This is the first step of [Trailblazer]'s journey among the starry seas. This place is called the Herta Space Station. Ummm... Just think of it as a supersized Grove of Epiphany.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Oh. So it's the territory of that witch. She and another Antikytheran lent me a helping hand back at the banquet.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Look, over there. Looks like [Trailblazer] is talking to Madam Herta in this memory.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let's go listen to what she thinks about this world, all constructed by Aeons and Paths...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Are you telling me THAT woman is Herta?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: She seems... shorter than I remember.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Pretty nice space station, huh, [Trailblazer]? But just wait. After a couple more stops on the Astral Express, you'll see sights that'll make this place look ordinary.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The cosmos is so vast that the "unknowns" far outnumber the "knowns," but none of them will end up being anything amazing. The farther you go, the more you'll understand what I mean.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: So do your best with the Nameless. Break a leg. And remember to send an update or two to Asta when you've got some downtime.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: She certainly shares my way of thinking...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Only that, instead of a conquest through blood and fire, they chose a gentler path.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: People call Madam Herta and Mister Screwllum "geniuses." Apparently, only the smartest people in the cosmos can receive the blessings of Nous, Amphoreus's true creator.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Do you mean that even individuals of such nobility are merely subordinates to a god?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: On the contrary, after all, it was the very first of them who created the god. But I don't really know all the details about that...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: You might be able to ask Madam Herta herself when you get the chance.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let's go check out some other worlds next, shall we?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: A snow-covered land? Interesting.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This star is named Jarilo-VI. Aww, that name sounds so cold... Belobog sounds better.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The girl we see here holds a similar station to you, Imperator. She's the Supreme Guardian of this world, a leader who took up the mantle of government during a disaster.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I did not expect the empress of this world to be so young.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Well, your appearance isn't much older...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: The object in the distance resembles {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}. Is it a weapon?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: No. It's called... Uhm... Right! The Geological Reconstruction Unit!
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Just {RUBY_B#Earth Titan}Georios{RUBY_E#}'s Titankin? Disappointing.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: It's all thanks to you that we survived the crisis. The collaboration with the IPC is both an opportunity and a challenge... Nonetheless, it's an important step in our journey back into the universe.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: This world was sealed beneath its sky just like Amphoreus was, and they only managed to reconnect with the stars when the Nameless arrived...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: That "IPC" she spoke of... Is it a more powerful organization?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Yes. The IPC conquered many worlds through trade and opened up a vast territory that way. There are many such powerful alliances beyond Amphoreus, and they all walk on roads different from the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Coming back to the Supreme Guardian and her Belobog... Didn't they find a peaceful way to enter the interstellar community?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: That cannot be true. That "IPC" would never have grown so big on trade alone. It may pretend to be a wealthy merchant with clean hands, but I am willing to bet that it grew fat on gory oppression and bloodshed.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Its path of conquest must have had no mercy for the weak and would have destroyed them if needed. Are you telling me that this snowland never thought about tossing its dignity to the wind and kneeling to the IPC? I will not believe it.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I will never allow the Imperator's empire to be sullied by others. Amphoreus must become a power so strong that no interstellar foreigner would dare to look down upon us.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Imperator... Belobog isn't as weak as you imagine. Listen.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: ...I indeed hesitated, but now I understand what we must do. Belobog must learn how to walk on her own, until she no longer needs the support of others, and can stand on her two feet among the stars.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Even if I may not live to see it, I believe such a day will surely come.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: They still have their dignity intact. One day, that hope will melt through the ice and help them into a prosperous tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: But the order of the cosmos is already set in stone. The old laws decree that only the strong survive, binding the weak in an unbroken chain, until they wither and turn to dust. Unless... they embrace the power of the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: We... No... Amphoreus must shatter the old law and become the new order among the stars.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Speaking of the Order... Another one of [Trailblazer]'s companions may be able to enlighten you further on that.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Let's go to the next page.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Huh... Such opulence does indeed evoke astonishment.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This world is called Penacony, an Eternal City built upon a land of dreams.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: It's also [Trailblazer]'s previous stop, where they went through a risky but exciting adventure.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I know what you want to do, sidekick. You want to use that Deliverer's memories to influence me and tilt the scales of law toward {M#him}{F#her} and the two geniuses.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Tell me about it, then. That man standing afar has wings on his head... I am truly curious.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I wish to gaze upon the views of the Reverie Hotel one more time, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'll be just a traveler when I come back here again. And perhaps, through a traveler's eyes, even the things I once knew so well will feel strangely different.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Before we go on, tell me this, sidekick. Throughout {M#his}{F#her} "trailblaze"...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Penacony is a land of the Harmony where all dreams and hopes merge and combine. It believes in unrestrained freedom, and that's how it lost itself in shallow delights...
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Then, this young man before you chose to rewrite its laws using the power of the Order, hoping to shape a dream-bound paradise of perfect happiness.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Yet the paradise of my dreams remains far away. Perhaps a brief journey with the Nameless can show me more possibilities in my search for paradise.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: As for what Penacony should look like, it'll be up to her... no, up to their "trailblazing" now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It sounds like this ideal kingdom is no more.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: That's right. The people chose to wake up at the end. You can't see tomorrow when drowning in sweet dreams.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: This individual's "Law" acknowledged only gods and constructs, leaving no space for humanity. And yet, the fact that he could accept defeat and resume his journey shows a rare self-awareness and clarity of mind.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You are also very self-aware, Imperator.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Then you must know that the world promised by the Destruction also has no place for "humanity."
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: I am indeed very aware of Lycurgus's honeyed words of deceit. I have seen enough. Take me back.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Then let's wrap up this trip down memory lane with one last scene.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: This... absolute wonder...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Isn't it pretty? That's our Amphoreus. Our world flows and meanders in this endless band of light.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Though we were born from the designs of the gods and are not yet truly alive... the Chrysos Heirs of Amphoreus still chose to stand against fate and carved a legend no different from that of humankind.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: Will you really renounce the heroes in this world's previous thirty million cycles, Imperator? Including even yourself? ...Will you bow to brutal destiny and allow that puppet master named the Destruction to have THEIR wish?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: You really saw right through me, Imperator.
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: How can one rule an empire if one is incapable of understanding people's minds?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I have decided on Law's final destination. However, before I move my next chess piece...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Was there ever a memory of the ocean?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The ocean... My cradle. My home.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: "You shall complete your conquest in the ocean at the boundaries of this world, and eternally slumber in the sound of tides..."
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: "You shall eternally slumber in the sound of tides, and complete your conquest in the ocean at the boundaries of this world..."
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Our prophecies aligned as flawlessly as a sea snake circling upon itself... an elegant loop, like a joyful hymn.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Like the circulating ocean current. Like our two fates. Like Amphoreus itself.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: The trial is over. So, tell me...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Who will own the divine authority of "Law"?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I won't give it to anyone.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I am the "Law." Why should I give my imperial crown to any other?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Both the Deliverer and the Theoros came from beyond the sky. They have no right to interfere with the lands I conquered with my own two hands. The "Law" of Amphoreus shall be determined by Amphoreus's master.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: What exactly did you see in the trial?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Everything. I saw everything regarding the rules of this world's operation. I saw the laws of extrapolation that Theoros spoke of... I saw the "Ultimate Protocol."
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: As long as I offer a sacrifice of equal weight, I can rewrite the laws of this world according to my will. I can turn good into evil, ugliness into beauty, and weakness into strength...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Fate gave me a very fair deal.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: One rule change... for the life of one demigod.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: What... are you planning to do?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: You can't guess? We can conquer the stars without relying on any power from beyond the sky. We just need to make some reasonable sacrifices.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Your ambitions have already made so many people give up their lives for the "Law"! And you're still not done!?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: I am determined for Amphoreus to stand on her own two feet among the stars.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: You are beyond reason... You think such a simple and hypocritical statement can justify your atrocities!?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: "There's no new without destroying the old." That's what you consider an atrocity? Ironic, for that is also the unchanging law of Amphoreus's revolutions.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Ever since the Flame-Chase prophecy resounded in the distance, fate has decreed for the Chrysos Heirs to ignite our blood and illuminate this dark age. People would still be puppets of the old dynasty if it weren't for my conquests.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: But your rule doesn't seem to be any different from your predecessors'. Bloodshed, tyranny, oppression...
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: You're making the same mistakes they did.
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Go and see everything for yourself! Go to any library I've built. Go listen to the rumors on every street corner. Go and witness how the Imperator crushed the old laws and forged new ones. Go and see what my conquests brought to this world.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I cleansed the Chrysos War's filth and mended all the conflicts left by the Era Bellica. I restored Okhema's might and allowed mortals and Chrysos Heirs to face each other as equals in the Council. I punished all sins and rewarded all achievements...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I smashed {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#}'s shackles, united humankind to save themselves, and started the Flame-Chase Era. That's what the Imperator has done in her glorious life.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: So, now, harken to my final words: History will eventually forget Cerydra, but it will never forget the Imperator's people or the Flame-Chase Era she began!
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "Final words"...?
rows.speaker: Hysilens

rows.text: Amphoreus is about to be destroyed. There's no time left for pointless debates.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: There is only one law I want to overturn to aid the final battle of deliverance, so I will only offer the life of one demigod...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: In the name of the Imperator, I command you one last time, Helektra.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Either sacrifice yourself for conquest, or pierce this tyrant's chest with your sword.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "Thus, the Imperator concluded her final speech."

"At the end of her life, at the last moment before she stepped onto the altar, she gave her most loyal subject the choice to decide fate, just as she promised her compatriots before her very first campaign."
"My blood flows in you now! Heroic compatriots, follow me, and we'll seize fate's reins!"
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "The Imperator fell. Some say that the Dux Gladiorum turned traitor and killed her liege. Some say that she imprisoned the tyrant in a shallow pond of water, then left... which meant the Imperator had to kill herself to rewrite the 'Law'..."
"There are countless stories about her death. All we can be sure of is, when the knight left the Vortex, the Imperator was still mumbling about their past conquests together..."
"...The beginning and the end of her existence."
Imperator! Wait! How could someone of your status come to the front lines? Let me be the flag-bearer.
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: The troops defending the pass to the west of the Grove. Have they surrendered?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: They ran as quickly as they could when they heard your name! The Golden Cocoon Pass is now in the First Legion's hands!
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: Good. What about the Dolosian militia?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The Third Legion set fire to the mountains and flattened everything west of the basin. They just need a few more days...
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: That is enough. We cannot afford to miss an opportunity for victory. Lastly, how many Ladonian cannons are left?
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: They are no more. The Second and Fourth Legions have destroyed them all.
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: Very good. They now have no way out, no reinforcements, and no artillery support. We will be able to liberate the Grove of Epiphany in the blink of an eye.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: We will launch the final charge one quint after the {RUBY_B#midnight}Curtain-Fall Hour{RUBY_E#} tomorrow. Remember, as long as the alliance's flag still flies on my shoulders, you must keep moving forward.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Take no prisoners among the enemy soldiers. All sages who resist are to be captured and tried according to martial law. And do not destroy any books. Now go! Notify the entire army!
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Understood! Those who are resolved to die, we salute you!
rows.speaker: "Dux Fragoris" Labienus

rows.text: Reporting in! The Mountain Dwellers are resisting fiercely, and the legendary "Mountainbreaker" has personally engaged in battle. Their formations are nigh impenetrable...
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: Then cease our frontal assault. Send scouts to all legions and tell them to retreat into the Tretos plains before the {RUBY_B#evening}Parting Hour{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Wha— Are you planning to surrender?
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: It's a strategic change of plans. The seismic walking dragon is enough for that battlefield.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Walking dragon... You mean that stupid beast Terravox? What can they even do?
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: Stupid? No. They are the wisest of all of {RUBY_B#Earth Titan}Georios{RUBY_E#}'s creations. Only they can perceive the currents of time.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Let them deal with their earthly brethren! We will advance and take the lead in defeating what remains of our enemy.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I will deliver the most fiery retribution for the humiliation they dealt us, and crown myself with a god-slaying wreath!
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: ...Understood. I'll see to it. Those who are resolved to die, we salute you!
rows.speaker: "Dux Brumalis" Seneca

rows.text: The Temple of the Three Fates sent a letter, Imperator.
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: They refused to surrender and said this letter is their last warning to us.
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: Hah...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Tell the commanding officers not to launch any attacks unless they receive the Imperator's handwritten approval. Disobedience will be punished by death.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Wh—What are you doing?
rows.speaker: "Dux Carminum" Verginia

rows.text: The priests of the Three Fates aren't soldiers, but politicians. Do not mistakenly believe they don't have a plan. These dying pests will wring out every idea from their brains all for short-sighted gain. They are much shrewder than we are.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I am inferior to them in that regard. They also have the prophecy to wield as a weapon, something I am not blessed with. Launching an unplanned attack will only disadvantage us, as all of Amphoreus will judge our actions...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Which means I will be heading to the battlefield myself, just as I have always done. This time, however, I will go alone. I will conduct secret negotiations to ensure fate is on our side.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Understood! The legions will make their preparations. Those who are resolved to die, we salute you!
rows.speaker: "Dux Helkolithist" Apollonius

rows.text: Why are we not allowed to march out with the army, Imperator?
rows.speaker: Dux Goldweaver Aglaea

rows.text: This will be a long voyage with no return. Those of you who bear the prophecy cannot come with me.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Why are you personally leading this battle if it's doomed to fail? The Flame-Chase Journey cannot be without a leader...
rows.speaker: Dux Goldweaver Aglaea

rows.text: That is correct. The empire will be without a head when the Imperator falls. But remember, as long as you seize the right opportunities, even a chaotic game will remain winnable.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: My departure will create a long staircase for you. You will understand what I mean when news of my death reaches your ears.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Cerydra... Is our journey about to be over?
rows.speaker: Dux Fatorum Tribbie

rows.text: Destroy the old laws and forge new ones... My conquest has reached its limits within the borders of Amphoreus. Since the prophecy already decreed that the Imperator would never conquer the stars as she wished, I will bow out here and try no more.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: More Chrysos Heirs bearing divine authority will be born, and many more heroes will arise...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Will they demand peace or war? Will they resist tyranny, or become the next Imperator? I do not care. The children of the future will decide for themselves.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Do not mourn for me. Anyone can kill the Imperator, but the only one who can truly destroy her...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Is Cerydra.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "At the end, I faithfully recorded the most important battles in the Imperator's life. Her conquest was about to be completed at this point in the story."
"However, for some reason, a memory suddenly entered my mind just as I was about to put down my pen."
"It was a journey on a fantastical train. I had the honor of having a heart-to-heart conversation with the Imperator under the stars, and I asked her this question at the end of that discussion..."
How do you want history to remember you? As a hero who gave up her life for the Flame-Chase... or as a tyrant?
rows.speaker: Cyrene

rows.text: "She answered so quickly, as if she had made up her mind long ago."
I would rather be forgotten than be defined.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Because the "Law" can be neither eternal nor unchallenged...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: And only "humanity" can pen laws into history's pages.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Now, I have shattered the greatest "Law" of Amphoreus...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: The game... is nearing its end...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Dux Gladiorum... even though... you killed the Imperator... in the previous thirty million cycles...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: This time... you finally... found your own "Law"...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Then... Hysilens... Helektra...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I will ask someone to deliver... the prophecy's "ocean at the boundaries of this world"... to you...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Will you... choose to... swim into that ocean...? I... do not care...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Do not... care...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "The Imperator muttered about her conquests, and news of her death spread in the city."
Freedom! Liberty! The tyrant is dead! Go, shout this news in the streets!
rows.speaker: Spirited Elder

rows.text: My people! My fellow Elders! Do not panic. Stand your ground. That tyrant has paid for her ambition with her life!
rows.speaker: Delighted Elder

rows.text: People once cheered for my ascension... and now they cheer for my fall... No matter. I am fond of applause...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Ah... I see... the cosmos... the battlefield that I cannot reach...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I will return... in the next cycle... The stars will hear my legion's war drums... hear... the great name of... the Imperator...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Hear... Amphoreus's...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: Cery... dra...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: "To this day, we do not know which rule the Imperator overwrote at the cost of her life."
"Perhaps the truth will only be revealed at the moment of checkmate, just like every chess game she ever played."

"We only know her death inflamed Okhema. On one side of the city, those who defended liberty toppled her statues to the ground. On the other side, her supporters put themselves between the masses and her monuments, declaring loudly that 'the sovereign is still among the people.'"
"It is said that golden blood congealed into the same letters everywhere they fought. It was the name borne by Okhema's first and final sovereign: the 'Imperator' Cerydra."
"But the one who bore that name did not see any of this. Her gaze was cast far away, and the sound of tides in her ears drowned out the people's cries."

"What was the Imperator thinking about in that prophesied 'ocean at the boundaries of this world'? In that shallow puddle of stagnant water? Was she reminiscing about her past conquests, or repenting for the millions killed for the Flame-Chase?"

"It was neither. The Imperator only saw how the surface of the water gleamed like that crude chessboard, dissected by light and shadow, in the afternoon when her teacher played against her for the first time."
Look at this chessboard. What do the pieces look like?
rows.speaker: Eccentric Chessmaster

rows.text: Heh. They are strangely beautiful...
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: They look like... the stars in the night sky ablaze.
rows.speaker: Cerydra

rows.text: I have to admit, the twelve factors' emulation of life in this experiment has far exceeded my expectations.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Make your choice then, Senior Society Member. Do you want to keep walking down the wrong path and be remembered for your incorrect conclusions...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Or do you want to return to the audience's seat and give yourself, Amphoreus, and the entire cosmos a more fitting end?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I must refuse. A dead man never fears death.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Did I not make myself clear? Have you forgotten about our dear {RUBY_B#Genius Society #4}"Lord of Silence"{RUBY_E#}? You wouldn't want her to consider your eight other clones as cancers within the Erudition and chop them all up, would you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Your logical deductions are vastly different from mine. Therefore, allow me to provide one more academic recommendation.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Listen, my peers. Why don't you look beyond this world, just as the Chrysos Heirs did? Re-evaluate your calculations, and take into account all enemies in the upcoming war among the Aeons.
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: Amphoreus is not a place where three Paths "entangle," but where three Paths "fight to the death."
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: You used memoria to resist me, but did you not consider the possibility that...
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: The Remembrance and THEIR children might have taken this opportunity to join the fray as well?
rows.speaker: "Zandar"

rows.text: In the meantime...
Ohh. So this isn't just silence. It's the answer.
"What was the last thing [Trailblazer] said to you before you parted the waters at the Scalegorge Waterscape?" ...A tricky question, but one with a simple answer.
That's correct. And now, I'm sure...
You are not March 7th. There's no way she would remember that detail.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'll only warn you once. Leave her body. Now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: How impulsive. That's not like you at all.
Why don't you calm down and think about another possibility? I didn't take over "March 7th's" body...
Rather, it's March 7th who regained "my" memories.
Memories are the prelude to dreams...
What are you talking about?
(Remain silent.)
